tasks.notes: locate — the factory lives under internal/bind among ~20 adapter files, not in the public Gson.java; requires navigating past the public API into the binding layer.

tasks.answer_key: gson/src/main/java/com/google/gson/internal/bind/EnumTypeAdapter.java (nameToConstant built in constructor ~L82-L102 reading @SerializedName value + alternate; read() ~L113 looks up the key)

tasks.prompt: Walk through what happens when application code calls gson.fromJson(json, MyType.class): how does Gson turn the JSON text into a MyType instance? Name the internal steps and the real classes/methods involved, from the public call down to the point where the JSON tokens are actually read.
tasks.success_criterion: Describes that Gson.fromJson wraps the input in a JsonReader, resolves a TypeAdapter for the target type via Gson.getAdapter(TypeToken), then calls TypeAdapter.read(JsonReader) which pulls tokens from the JsonReader to construct the object.
tasks.answer_key: 1) Gson.fromJson(String/Reader, Type) constructs a com.google.gson.stream.JsonReader over the input. 2) It calls Gson.getAdapter(TypeToken<T>) (Gson.java ~L340) to obtain the TypeAdapter<T> for the requested type (cached; built by registered TypeAdapterFactories such as ReflectiveTypeAdapterFactory). 3) It invokes TypeAdapter.read(JsonReader) (abstract, TypeAdapter.java ~L309; the public entry TypeAdapter.fromJson ~L211 delegates here). 4) The adapter's read() consumes tokens from the JsonReader (JsonReader.java: doPeek/nextString/nextName/beginObject etc.) to build and return the T instance. Gson.fromJson then verifies the reader is exhausted and returns the object.
tasks.notes: explain — comprehension of the deserialization pipeline; judge-graded. Key files: Gson.java (fromJson + getAdapter), TypeAdapter.java (read/fromJson), stream/JsonReader.java (token source).
